comparisons.peer_summary: As of December 31, 2024, loans increased by $19.8 billion due to higher loans in CIB and securities-based lending in AWM, while lending-related commitments decreased by $5.3 billion due to decreases in AWM and CCB, largely offset by higher commitments in CIB.
comparisons.comparison: Both Bank of America and JPMorgan Chase disclose growth in their securities-based lending portfolios as a key driver for overall loan expansion in 2024. BAC reports that its direct/indirect consumer portfolio increased by $3.7 billion, with this growth explicitly attributed to 'increases in securities-based lending and consumer auto' (bac_2024_7_P309_S002). Similarly, JPM states that its total loans increased by $19.8 billion, 'driven by higher loans in CIB and higher securities-based lending in AWM' (jpm_2024_7_P534_S001). While BAC breaks out its securities-based lending within a specific 'direct/indirect consumer' bucket (constituting 49% of that $107.1 billion portfolio), JPM identifies it as a primary growth vector across its consolidated loan book within the Asset & Wealth Management segment.

sentences.text: Outstandings in the direct/indirect portfolio increased $3.7 billion in 2024 to $107.1 billion driven by increases in securities-based lending and consumer auto.

At December 31, 2024, 51 percent of the direct/indirect portfolio was included in Consumer Banking (consumer auto and recreational vehicle lending) and 49 percent was included in GWIM (principally securities-based lending loans).
As of December 31, 2024, loans increased $19.8 billion, driven by higher loans in CIB and higher securities-based lending in AWM.

comparisons.peer_topic: Wealth Management CRE Lending Portfolio Overview and Risk Profile
comparisons.peer_summary: As of December 31, 2024, direct lending against CRE properties in Wealth Management totaled $7.7 billion, representing 4.3% of total exposure and primarily included in Securities-based lending and Other loans. These loans are originated through the private banking platform, secured, and over 95% benefit from guarantees from high net worth clients, with all lending located in the Americas.
comparisons.comparison: Both Bank of America and Morgan Stanley disclose the composition and nature of securities-based lending within their wealth management or consumer portfolios. BAC states that 49% of its direct/indirect consumer portfolio, totaling roughly $52.5 billion (calculated from the $107.1 billion total), is included in GWIM as 'principally securities-based lending loans' (bac_2024_7_P309_S001). Morgan Stanley reports $7.7 billion in direct lending against CRE properties within its Wealth Management segment, noting that this exposure is 'primarily included within Securities-based lending and Other loans' (ms_2024_7_P360_S002). Both firms highlight securities-based lending as a significant component of their wealth/client lending offerings, though BAC provides a precise percentage of a larger direct/indirect bucket, while MS aggregates CRE lending into that category with a smaller absolute balance.

sentences.text: At December 31, 2024, 51 percent of the direct/indirect portfolio was included in Consumer Banking (consumer auto and recreational vehicle lending) and 49 percent was included in GWIM (principally securities-based lending loans).

This represents 4.3% and 4.3%, respectively, of total exposure reflected in the Wealth Management Loans and Lending Commitments table above, primarily included within Securities-based lending and Other loans.
